setting: A rugged Canadian Shield woodland beside a small lake: rock ridges, mixed forest, a beaver-influenced shoreline and a protected wetland
units: metres; x east, y south, origin at the north-west corner of the map

provenance.source: Entirely invented for discussion from a written landscape description. No cadastral, topographic, lidar, photographic or environmental survey is represented, and no real property was consulted.
provenance.method: A seeded elevation function (base rise, Gaussian ridges and hollows, deterministic roughness, small graded building benches) drives contours, hillshade, slope checks and the view assessment. The same seed and functions are used for every generated output.

roughness.note: Low deterministic roughness breaks up the smooth hill shapes. It is not a surveyed surface and contains no rock, soil or drainage information.

building_pads.note: Illustrative levelled benches cut into the slope under each building. Real foundations need a geotechnical investigation, grading design and erosion and sediment control. A pad is a design assumption, not permission to excavate.

terrain.note: A smooth invented surface with seeded roughness and small building benches for illustration. Real siting needs a topographic survey, soils, hydrology and rock assessment.

lake.name: Heron Lake
lake.type: small Canadian Shield lake with a beaver-influenced inlet
lake.beaver_note: A low earth-and-brush dam at the southern inlet is implied by the water level and the wet meadow beyond it. Nothing is drawn as an engineered dam, and no trapping, clearing or water-level management is proposed.
lake.note: The shoreline is a smooth illustrative curve, not a surveyed water's edge. In Ontario, the bed of a lake may be Crown land and the shoreline may be regulated. Confirm title, survey and approvals.

wetland.name: Beaver meadow
wetland.connection: Seasonally connected to the lake by two drainage channels. The wet meadow is the low, open ground behind the implied beaver dam.
wetland.note: Illustrative wetland only. A real wetland boundary needs a qualified ecologist and may be provincially significant and regulated.

drainage.name: Ridge drainage channel
drainage.note: Seasonal flow from the north ridge to the wet meadow. Paths cross on a proposed culvert or step-over; no filling is assumed.

drainage.name: West drainage channel
drainage.note: Seasonal flow from the north-west woods to the lake. The lower reach is inside the shoreline buffer and is left undisturbed.

parcel.note: Drawn to the water's edge for simplicity. Many Canadian shorelines include a shore road allowance or Crown land: check title and survey. The eastern boundary is a fictional road frontage.

no_build.applies_to: buildings, porches, ramps, parking and crane pads. Lanes and walking paths stay out of the shoreline and wetland buffers. They may cross a seasonal drainage channel only on a designed culvert or step-over; rock outcrops are avoided rather than cut.
no_build.note: Illustrative planning assumptions, not legal setbacks. 30 m is a common minimum in Canadian municipal plans, but requirements vary by province, municipality and wetland significance and can be much larger. Rock and drainage buffers are project choices for this fiction. Confirm every distance with the planning authority and the conservation authority or provincial regulator. A constraint analysis does not establish development permission.

woodland.name: Mixed Shield woodland
woodland.note: Indicative stands and canopy, not a forest inventory. Dominant species are suggested from the fictional terrain and moisture, not observed. No tree is proposed for removal until an arborist and ecologist have assessed the site.

stands.name: North ridge pine and spruce
stands.note: Thin rocky soils on the ridge: white pine, red pine and spruce with a sparse understory.

stands.name: Central mixed wood
stands.note: Sugar maple, yellow birch, beech, hemlock and white pine on deeper ground between rock outcrops.

stands.name: South birch and cedar
stands.note: White birch, trembling aspen and eastern white cedar near the wet ground, with speckled alder at the meadow edge.

stands.name: Shoreline cedar and pine
stands.note: Cedar, balsam fir and white pine hold the shore. This stand is left uncut and is the main winter screening for the lake-facing homes.

stands.name: East mixed woodland
stands.note: Additional mixed woodland on the eastern edge of the fictional 15-acre parcel. Indicative only.

rocks.name: North ridge outcrop
rocks.note: Exposed granite and lichen with shallow moss pockets. No building, blasting or drilling is assumed.

rocks.name: East outcrop
rocks.note: A low east-facing rock shelf, kept as a landscape feature near the entrance.

rocks.name: South knoll outcrop
rocks.note: A rock shoulder above the wet meadow. The buffer is a planning assumption, not a geotechnical finding.

rocks.name: Shore outcrop
rocks.note: A small outcrop inside the shoreline buffer, left as wildlife habitat and a landing for amphibians.

rocks.name: North outcrop
rocks.note: A low outcrop near the north boundary, used as a reference point for the ridge walk.

clearings.name: Gathering glade
clearings.note: A small natural opening west of the lodge for outdoor meals, a fire circle and children's play. No additional clearing is proposed.

clearings.name: Birch glade
clearings.note: A sunlit opening in the birch stand, viewed from Cabin B's screened porch and used as a shared picnic spot.

entrance.name: Primary entrance from the public road
entrance.note: One entrance only. A locked gate or bollard is assumed at the road; emergency services receive access details.

lanes.name: Gravel access lane from the public road
lanes.note: Short entrance lane. Daily traffic ends at the shared parking area.

lanes.name: North emergency, construction and maintenance track
lanes.surface: grass-pave or reinforced turf, normally closed to daily traffic
lanes.note: A narrow woodland track for fire response, module delivery and maintenance. It crosses the ridge drainage channel on a proposed culvert; capacity, erosion control and winter maintenance to be designed. It is not the daily route to any home.

lanes.name: West emergency spur
lanes.note: Reaches Cabin F and the south-west homes. The turnaround is a reinforced-turf pad, not a paved cul-de-sac.

lanes.name: South emergency track
lanes.note: A second narrow branch north of the wet meadow. It stays outside the 30 m wetland buffer and crosses the ridge drainage channel on a proposed culvert.

lanes.name: East emergency spur
lanes.note: Reaches Cabin E. No permanent widening is assumed.

parking.note: A modest shared parking area at the edge of the site. Three accessible spaces and an accessible drop-off sit nearest the lodge ramp. Homes are reached on foot. Parking is not allocated to individual homes.

dropoff.name: Accessible drop-off
dropoff.note: A level drop-off beside the lodge entry ramp, usable by a car, a small shuttle or a utility cart.

trails.name: Accessible arrival path
trails.note: Short level route from the drop-off to the lodge entry ramp. Gradient and cross-fall to be designed.

trails.name: Lodge glade path
trails.note: From the lodge's screened porch to the gathering glade.

trails.name: West woodland path
trails.note: The main walking route from the lodge into the west woods. It stays behind the homes and never runs along the lake shore.

trails.name: Ridge path to Cabin B
trails.note: Approaches Cabin B from the south-west, then turns to its north entrance. It does not cross the birch-glade view.

trails.name: Cabin A path
trails.note: Arrives from the east at the north entry. The south-west porch and its lake view are left uninterrupted.

trails.name: Cabin C path
trails.note: A short link from the west spine to Cabin C's east entry.

trails.name: South woodland path
trails.note: A dry route north of the wet meadow, outside the 30 m buffer. It approaches Cabin D from the north, away from its wetland view.

trails.name: Cabin E path
trails.note: A short spur from the west spine to Cabin E's east entry.

trails.name: Cabin F path
trails.note: Approaches Cabin F from the north-east. The lake-facing porch is left private, and the path crosses a drainage channel on a proposed culvert.

circulation.note: Lane widths, turnarounds, gradients, surfacing and the distance limit are placeholders. Confirm fire department access requirements, load ratings, winter maintenance and emergency response with the authority having jurisdiction. The emergency track is not a substitute for a fire access route designed to local standards.

crane.note: Placeholder reach from a temporary crane standing point to the module centre. Lifts are made from reinforced temporary matting beside the emergency track; no permanent crane pad is built. Real limits depend on crane, outriggers, module weight, ground bearing, rock and the lift plan. No lifts over the wetland or shoreline buffers.

buildings.name: Cabin A
buildings.clearing_note: A small opening in the cedar and pine, just large enough for the home, its porch and a few sunlit shrubs. The forest edge is left ragged.

orientation.reason: The long side and screened porch turn south-west across the slope to the lake, while the entry and path stay on the north-east side.

main.description: Heron Lake seen through cedar and pine, with the far shore low on the horizon.
main.through: shoreline cedar, white pine and a few birch

secondary.description: The north ridge and its rock outcrops rise behind the home, catching late light.

views.nearby: Cabin B is about 90 m east along the ridge and is screened by pine; Cabin C is about 60 m south-east and largely hidden by the slope.
views.path: The walking path arrives from the east at the north entry. No path crosses the south-west porch or its lake view.
views.winter: Cedar and pine keep the lake edge screened in winter. Leaf-off opens a clearer view through the birch, and the low sun reaches the porch.

buildings.design_note: Cabin A's one-module plan is the starting point. A site-specific variant would widen the sleeping room to fit a 1.5 m turning circle and choose the porch screen colour with the resident.
buildings.character: A cedar-screened bench above the lake, with the porch turned to the water and the entry tucked behind.
buildings.design_lab_note: Illustrative architectural assignment for the Phase 2 comparison. The authoritative site geometry and the separate Cabin A and lodge models are unchanged.

buildings.name: Cabin B
buildings.clearing_note: A small bench clearing on the ridge shoulder. The birch glade beyond it is left open and is shared, not private garden.

orientation.reason: The home turns its porch south-east toward the birch glade and the ridge, away from the main lake and away from its neighbours.

main.description: A sunlit birch glade and a low rock shoulder, with the forest floor visible beneath the trunks.
main.through: white birch, maple and scattered pine

secondary.description: A partial lake glimpse to the west through the ridge pines, strongest in winter.

views.nearby: Cabin E is about 57 m south-east and may be glimpsed through birch in winter; the lodge roof is about 85 m east. Cabin A is about 104 m west behind the ridge.
views.path: The ridge path comes from the south-west and turns to the north entry, keeping the birch-glade view clear.
views.winter: Birch and maple lose their leaves, opening the glade and the lake glimpse. The pines behind the home still screen the ridge track.

buildings.design_note: A two-bedroom variant could use two modules on this wider bench. The current one-module concept is shown as a placeholder for the resident's own brief.
buildings.character: A ridge-top home that looks into a sunlit birch glade rather than at the water.
buildings.design_lab_note: Illustrative architectural assignment for the Phase 2 comparison. The authoritative site geometry and the separate Cabin A and lodge models are unchanged.

buildings.name: Cabin C
buildings.clearing_note: A quiet opening in the central mixed wood, surrounded by mature pine and hemlock. The clearing is kept small so the forest closes around the home.

orientation.reason: The porch faces almost due west along a long forest corridor to the lake. The entry and path are on the east side, out of the view.

main.description: A long view west between pine trunks to a narrow strip of lake, more water than sky.
main.through: mature white pine, hemlock and maple

secondary.description: The north ridge shows through the canopy to the right of the porch.

views.nearby: Cabin A is about 57 m north-west and may be glimpsed through the pines in winter; Cabin E is about 76 m north-east and screened by mixed wood.
views.path: The path leaves the west spine and arrives at the east entry. Bedroom and living windows face west and south, away from it.
views.winter: Pine and hemlock hold their needles, so the long view stays framed but private. Leaf-off reveals more of the lake and the ridge.

buildings.design_note: The resident might replace the west trellis with a small covered deck. The landscape model accepts that change without moving the home.
buildings.character: A quiet room in the pines, with a long view west between trunks.
buildings.design_lab_note: Illustrative architectural assignment for the Phase 2 comparison. The authoritative site geometry and the separate Cabin A and lodge models are unchanged.

buildings.name: Cabin D
buildings.clearing_note: A small dry rise at the edge of the wet meadow, with moss, lowbush blueberry and cedar. No fill is placed in the meadow.

orientation.reason: The porch faces south-south-west over the beaver meadow, while the entry and path stay on the north side, away from the wetland.

main.description: The beaver meadow: open sedge, alder and standing water, with the south knoll and its rock shoulder beyond.
main.through: alder, cedar and low meadow vegetation

secondary.description: The south knoll and a rock shoulder catch the afternoon sun above the meadow.

views.nearby: Cabin E is about 45 m north-east and screened by cedar; the lodge is about 45 m north and partly visible through trees in winter.
views.path: The south path approaches from the north and ends at the north entry. It stays outside the 30 m wetland buffer, so nobody walks between the porch and the meadow.
views.winter: The meadow opens completely when the alder drops its leaves, and the low sun reaches the porch. Cedar on the east side screens the lodge.

buildings.design_note: A seasonal home might use a smaller, simpler service core and a larger screened room. The wetland view is the reason for this site; the building should stay modest.
buildings.character: A seasonal camp at the meadow edge, turned toward the beaver meadow and the south knoll.
buildings.design_lab_note: Illustrative architectural assignment for the Phase 2 comparison. The authoritative site geometry and the separate Cabin A and lodge models are unchanged.

buildings.name: Cabin E
buildings.clearing_note: A ferny opening between rock and mixed wood, close enough to the lodge for a short walk but screened from it by a cedar clump.

orientation.reason: The porch turns west into the fern and hemlock understory, with a lake glimpse beyond. The entrance is on the east, toward the lodge and the path.

main.description: Fern, hemlock and a distant plane of lake light. The view is more forest than water.

secondary.description: The east rock shelf and the entrance clearing sit behind the home, seen from the path rather than the porch.

views.nearby: Cabin C is about 76 m west-south-west and may be glimpsed through fern and hemlock; Cabin A is about 110 m west across the slope. The lake light dominates the view.
views.path: The east spur reaches the east entry. The porch, bedroom and living windows face west, away from the lodge and the path.
views.winter: Hemlock and cedar keep the lodge screened. Leaf-off opens the lake glimpse and makes the east rock shelf more visible from the path.

buildings.design_note: As the community rental, this home needs robust finishes and a locked owner's store. The model can accept a second entrance without changing the landscape.
buildings.character: A small rental tucked into fern and hemlock, a short walk from the lodge.
buildings.design_lab_note: Illustrative architectural assignment for the Phase 2 comparison. The authoritative site geometry and the separate Cabin A and lodge models are unchanged.

buildings.name: Cabin F
buildings.clearing_note: A low juniper and blueberry opening above the southern shore, small enough to leave the shoreline cedar uncut.

orientation.reason: The porch faces west-south-west to the lake across the southern cove. The entry is on the east and the path arrives from the north-east.

main.description: The southern cove of Heron Lake through juniper and cedar, with the opposite shore close enough to read the rock.

secondary.description: The wet meadow and its alder thicket lie to the south-east, visible from the path but not the porch.

views.nearby: Cabin C is about 60 m north and hidden by the shore knoll; no other home is visible from the porch.
views.path: The Cabin F path arrives from the north-east at the east entry. It crosses a seasonal drainage channel on a proposed culvert and stays out of the shoreline buffer.
views.winter: Cedar and juniper keep the cove private. The lake opens wider in winter, and the low sun reaches the porch through the bare birch.

buildings.design_note: This is the smallest-feeling site and may suit a seasonal, one-person or couple's home. A future 20-foot module variant could be tested here without changing the clearing.
buildings.character: A low, juniper-edged retreat above the southern cove.
buildings.design_lab_note: Illustrative architectural assignment for the Phase 2 comparison. The authoritative site geometry and the separate Cabin A and lodge models are unchanged.

buildings.name: Common lodge
buildings.clearing_note: A modest opening at the arrival edge of the site, large enough for the lodge, its two ramps and the gathering glade beyond. The forest closes behind it.

orientation.reason: The screened porch and gathering hall face west into the gathering glade, while the entry, drop-off and accessible ramp face east toward the parking area.

main.description: The gathering glade and the mixed forest beyond, seen from the screened porch and the hall's west glazing.
main.through: maple, birch and hemlock at the edge of the glade

secondary.description: The east rock shelf and the arrival clearing are seen from the entry and the accessible path, not from the gathering space.

views.nearby: Cabin E is about 41 m west-south-west and may be glimpsed at the edge of the glade through cedar; Cabin C is about 112 m west and only visible in winter.
views.path: The accessible arrival path comes from the drop-off to the east ramp. The glade path leaves the west porch. Neither crosses a home's private view.
views.winter: Hemlock and cedar keep the glade edge green in winter. The hall's clerestories bring low winter light into the gathering space, and the porch stays usable with screens and a windbreak.

buildings.design_note: The lodge is the social centre, so it gets the most accessible arrival, the universal washroom, the shared kitchen and the workshop. It is deliberately at the edge, near parking and services, not in the quietest part of the woods.
buildings.character: The shared hearth: kitchen, hall, workshop and the gathering glade.
buildings.design_lab_note: Illustrative architectural assignment for the Phase 2 comparison. The authoritative site geometry and the separate Cabin A and lodge models are unchanged.

landmarks.name: North ridge
landmarks.note: The highest continuous ground, with shallow soil and exposed rock.

landmarks.name: South knoll
landmarks.note: A low rock shoulder above the wet meadow.

landmarks.name: East rock shelf
landmarks.note: A low east-facing outcrop near the entrance.

landmarks.name: Birch glade
landmarks.note: A sunlit opening in the birch stand.

landmarks.name: Gathering glade
landmarks.note: A small shared opening west of the lodge.

trees.note: Indicative canopy only, not a tree survey. Scatter is deterministic. Trees are kept out of water, wetland, rocks, building clearings, paths, lanes, parking and crane mats. No clearing is proposed beyond footprints, paths, the existing glades and the small building benches.

ecology: Heron Lake shoreline and beaver-influenced inlet
access: one vehicle entrance from the public road; shared parking and accessible drop-off at the lodge; daily circulation on foot; a narrow emergency, construction and maintenance track; no private driveways and no road to any individual home
note: The site is entirely fictional. It is a design hypothesis, not a surveyed parcel, environmental assessment, development application or offer of land.
